We have deleted the letters marked and read with a line through them.
And in this yellow, we have replaced.

You can count that there are 28 characters which have been inserted including spaces and

18 characters have been deleted and two characters have been substituted.
So, now, this can be a basis of measuring how close two documents are to each other.
So, the added distance is the minimum number of edit operations required to transform one
document to another.
So, we have to define what we mean by an edit operation.
So, let us just start with very basic operation.
Either you can insert a character or you can delete a character or you can replace one
character by another one in one step.
So, replacing of course, could be thought of as deleting and inserting.
So, that would be a two step operation.
I delete the character and then I insert the character I want.
But I am going to allow changing one letter A by B or S by T as a single operation.
So, in our example, we claim that 28 characters were inserted, 18 were deleted and two were
substituted.
So, the total number of changes we made is 48.
If the edit distance is supposed to be the minimum number of changes, it cannot be more
than 48 because they already shown that it is possible to do in 45.
Perhaps it is possible to do it in more clever way in less than 48.
So, the edit distance at most 48 for the two sentences that we showed earlier.
So, this distance is also called the Levenstein distance because it was first proposed by
then Soviet, now Russian scientist called Vladimir Levenstein.
And this like the longest common sub sequence problem is extremely useful in practice.
So, the first thing is to suggest spelling corrections.
Now, if somebody type something that is wrong, then a spelling character will have to suggest
the correct word from the dictionary to replace it.
So, which word should the spelling character choose?
So, one criterion for choosing is to identify among all the words in the dictionary that
are possible, which one is closest to the one that has been typed.
So, this can be measured in terms of this edit distance and then the manual pop-up saying
do you mean to type this?
This also happens when you type queries and search engines.
So, if you type something to Google, Google will sometimes change your query to a word
which is meaningful because it recognizes that you have mistyped a name or a concept.
We also said that the longest common sub sequence problem that we saw earlier is useful in
genetics and bioinformatics.
And in the same way edit distance also if we want to compare the genetic information into
different species, then it is natural to compare them in terms of the content of the DNA
and DNA are just long strings.
So, we want to find out how easy or difficult it is to transform one piece of DNA into
another and depending on that we can tell whether two species are close to each other or not.
